symptom: `alter microflow … insert` with `@annotation(id: n1)` meant to attach the new activity to a note already in the flow was refused at exec — '@annotation(id: n1) refers to an annotation that has not been declared — the first mention must carry the text' — while check passed it as 'not predicted'; there was no other way to attach a fragment statement to a stored note
cause: A fragment is built by a fresh flowBuilder whose annotationsByLabel starts empty, and the `id:` labels describe prints (n1, n2, …) are re-derived on every describe and stored nowhere, so there is nothing for a fragment to resolve them against. check only learned of the builder's error in alterFlowViolations' pre-build loop, which files builder errors as dependencies ('not predicted') rather than refusals
fix: New key `@annotation(existing: 'text')`: resolveStoredNotes (called by plan for exec and before the pre-build loop for check) resolves each text to exactly one stored note or refuses, listing the candidates with position and attachments; the builder links the stored note's ID; the lines are taken out of the fragment and drawn by MicroflowMutator.LinkNote after the splice, oriented with microflows.FacingSides (moved there from the executor so builder and splice share one formula) on the post-splice geometry. ValidateAlterFlow now also runs checkAnnotationLabels per fragment, so an undeclared `id:` is refused by check (MDL079) with a hint at `existing:`
insight: Two traps beyond the obvious. (1) Any refusal that lives in the fragment BUILDER is downgraded by check to 'not predicted — exec decides' (alterFlowViolations treats builder errors as dependencies on earlier statements), so a deterministic refusal must be decided before the build, by a function both plan and alterFlowViolations call. (2) A line from a stored note cannot ride in the fragment: the builder never knew where the stored note is relative to what it builds (sides come out as the bottom→top default), withoutNotes/singleActivity treat a line to a non-fragment object as a non-note so the error-handler and loop-body in-place replaces refuse, and Replace carries the target's own line to the entry so the same note gets two lines. Drawing it after the splice via a mutator op that dedupes and orients on current geometry fixes all three; each was shown by a revert (lines left in the fragment: origin 2/destination 0 instead of 0/2, and 2 lines on replace). Address by text, not by the describe-time id: the id is a derived name that moves (docs-wiki/bug-patterns/mutator-addressing.md); text is what the canvas shows, and the miss/ambiguity message lists the notes so a mismatch is visible
